statements.title: Table I: the certified statements used in the paper (Lean 4, commit 42f307b) and their status in the literature
statements.formal_part: the statements of Table I (twenty Lean names), each checked by the Lean kernel in the public repository (commit 42f307b); the «status» column is the paper’s reading of the literature, not a Lean statement

statements.title: Margolus–Levitin: π ≤ 2⟨E⟩τ for a state that becomes orthogonal at τ
Mandelstam–Tamm, L¹ form: 1 ≤ D₁τ ≤ ΔE·τ
Zieliński–Zych: π^α ≤ 2M_α τ^α for every α > 0
two-level drive: τ ≥ π/Ω_max for every pulse shape; a fixed-axis π pulse has speed-limit ratio exactly 1
statements.formal_part: constant Rabi frequency: Margolus–Levitin. Time-dependent drive: (i) piecewise-constant evolutions with spectral width at most Ω_max move any state by a Fubini–Study angle at most (Ω_max/2)T; (ii) fixed-axis drive: equality case of the generalized Mandelstam–Tamm bound; (iii) transfer to fidelity 1−ε: Ω_max T ≥ 2 arccos √ε. Continuous pulses are covered only as limits of piecewise-constant ones (not formalized).

statements.title: entangling time in any local dimension: arccos λ ≤ J·Στ_k
a Bell vector needs J·Στ_k ≥ π/4, in any local dimension d ≥ 2
the bound is attained: H = J·Z⊗X reaches a Bell vector in time π/(4J)
the earlier chord-distance version: J·Στ_k ≥ √(2−√2) ≈ 0.7654
any CNOT, or gate locally equivalent to it (ECR), on the qubit subspace of two d-level systems needs J·T ≥ π/4
statements.formal_part: the Bell-vector bound and its extension to (P⊗Q)·Bell, which covers every gate only locally equivalent to CNOT (ECR); the CNOT consequence itself is the Bell bound applied to |+⟩|0⟩

statements.title: robust bounds: a Bell vector to fidelity 1−ε needs J·Στ_k ≥ π/4 − arcsin √ε; a two-level transfer needs Ω_max T ≥ 2 arccos √ε
the drive convention is c = 1: IBM’s calibrated π pulse rotates by 1.148 π with c = 1 (2.296 π with c = 2)
the residual is explained: omegad·|amp|·A_rec = π on all 777 qubits to 1.2·10⁻⁷; the ratio of the two areas tends to 1/(1−e⁻²) = 1.15652
omegad is not an independent measurement: IBM derives it from the π-pulse calibration
the pre-registered falsifier fired on 254 qubits of three backends with placeholder-like values, which are excluded
X gates last a median 11.30 times their two-level speed limit at full drive amplitude
what sets the duration: the gap factors into a pulse shape (≈ 2.16 = 1.87 × 1/(1−e⁻²)) and an amplitude reserve (≈ 5)
pre-registered rivals: H1 rejected at full amplitude (depends on the waveform reading at the drive used), H3 excluded, H2 without support
IBM’s design rule: the calibrated peak Rabi frequency is about 0.09 of the anharmonicity (0.0907, or 0.078 with the normalized peak)
per-qubit durations under the cap would gain only ×1.09; cairo runs above the cap
1758 coupled pairs in 43 backends: median j_q = 0.01268 rad/ns, median gate 548 ns
ECR/CX gates last a median 4.22 times the CNOT-class bound π/(2j_q)
against our certified constants the median ratio is 8.7 (chord) or 8.4 (sharp π/4), twice the literature one
statements.formal_part: the two bounds; the ratios (8.7 chord, 8.4 sharp, and ≈ 16.9 with the second level) are computations on vendor data, not Lean statements

statements.title: numerical controls of the certified bound: 0 violations in 20 000 and 3000 trials
cross resonance against its first-order formula: median θ/(π/2) = 1.109; Ω_CR/Δ ≈ 0.45
single-qubit ratio frozen near 11 from 2021 to 2025; two-qubit ratio 2.78 → 4.26
the two-qubit ratio grew because gates got longer, not because the coupling changed
lengthening does not lower the error: Spearman +0.13 (p = 0.23); it falls in only 31 % of lengthened pairs
a pooled effect (p = 0.0017) vanished under a stratified control (p = 0.90): consistent with confounding by epoch
optimal control: shortest X time found ≈ max(π/Ω_max, ~1.1·2π/|δ|), a speed-limit branch and a leakage-dominated branch
a lower bound for any number of levels: T ≥ π/Ω_max, and in the trace metric T ≥ 2 arcsin(1−e)/Ω_max; for r ≤ 0.2 the times found are 6 % above it
for IBM’s |δ| ≈ 2.07 rad/ns: the fastest pulse found takes ≈ 16 ns at its own cap (35.6 ns is ≈ 2.2 times that); at r = 1 the 4-level search finds 3.3 ns, but that value is truncation-dependent
truncation: the 4-level pulse at r = 1 degrades to 5.5–7.2·10⁻⁴ with 5 to 12 levels; a 6-level pulse at T = 7.0/|δ| (3.4 ns) reaches 4.0·10⁻⁶ there and 3.6·10⁻⁶ with 8 and 12 levels

the full amplitude |D| = 1 is r_full = omegad/|δ|, median 0.351; at r = 0.351 an X of 4.8 ns exists (bound 4.3 ns): the median gate is 10–11 times the model minimum, a 35.6 ns Falcon gate 7.4–8.3 times
cross resonance: the fastest CNOT found is ≈ 1.2 times slower at IBM’s drive fraction 0.45 than at 0.7
CZ with the second transmon level: error 2·10⁻⁸ at T = 0.55/J with local controls ≤ 10J, i.e. 0.35 of the qubit-only time and 5 % above the construction π/(6J)
statements.formal_part: the entangling-time bound (J = ‖H_c‖ = 2J for d = 3, giving π/(8J)), its robust form with tolerance ε and the 97/32 lemma of the refined bound (QSL.Exchange.refined_cz_lemma; see r:czrefined); the CZ solutions themselves are numerical witnesses, not Lean statements

statements.title: explicit CZ construction: fast twirling of one transmon keeps (J/2)Q⊗Q, the code in the extreme eigenvectors of Q gives (3J/2)Z⊗Z and a CZ in π/(6J) = 0.5236/J; so π/(8J) ≤ T_* ≤ π/(6J), and with the refined bound (next nodes) 0.4511/J ≤ T_* ≤ π/(6J)
statements.formal_part: only the lower bound π/(8J) (entangling-time theorem with ‖H_c‖ = 2J, d = 3); the upper bound, the explicit construction, is not formalized

statements.title: a gate bound by the Choi state: T_*(e) ≥ [π/4 − arccos(1−e)]/(2J), so 0.392599/J ≤ T_*(2·10⁻⁸) ≤ 0.55/J (sharpened to 0.4510/J in r:czrefined); exact Bell preparation is a different, easier task
statements.formal_part: the tolerance theorem (ε the infidelity of one output state); its instantiation with two-level references on each transmon, which turns it into a bound on the gate in the trace metric, is ours and not formalized

statements.title: a refined CZ bound: T_* ≥ 0.4511/J (a comparator-trajectory argument; the 97/32 lemma is certified in Lean), so 0.4511/J ≤ T_* ≤ π/(6J) = 0.5236/J and T_*(2·10⁻⁸) ≥ 0.4510/J
statements.formal_part: the lemma (1/4)·Tr[(P_A⊗P_B)H_c²] ≤ (97/32)J² for rank-2 projectors on d = 3, and its equality case at P = 1 − |v⟩⟨v|, |v⟩ = √(7/8)|0⟩ + √(1/8)|2⟩; the time argument built on it (the comparator trajectory L(t), the Fubini–Study speed, the distance π/4 from the product states) is not formalized

statements.title: version 3: two copies give T_* ≥ π/(√46 J) = 0.4632/J; a closed excursion through |mm⟩, certified in interval arithmetic, gives T_* ≤ 0.520023/J; so the CZ lies between 0.295 and 0.331 of the qubit-only time

larger local dimension: the construction gives a CZ in π/(2Jλ_d²), the entangling-time theorem gives π/(4Jκ_d); the ratio 2κ_d/λ_d² is 2, 1.33, 1.27, 1.20, 1.09, 1.05 for d = 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 20 and tends to 1
statements.formal_part: λ_d²/2 ≤ κ_d ≤ 2(d−1) (exchange_norm_ge, exchange_norm_le), λ_d ≥ 2(1 − 1/m)√(d − m) for the largest eigenvalue (lamMax_ge) and 2κ_d/λ_d² → 1 (ratio_tendsto_one), in Formalizations/Physics/QuantumMechanics/SpeedLimit/ExchangeQuadrature.lean; the rate O(d^(−2/3)) (asymptotics of the largest Hermite zero, DLMF 18.16.17), the d-level CZ construction itself and the table of ratios are not formalized

statements.title: Heisenberg coupling and ancillas: the smallest largest-Schmidt-coefficient is exactly cos(2T) up to the Bell time π/8 (an analytic witness)
statements.formal_part: the lower bound: arccos λ ≤ T‖H − c1‖ for every real c, and the Heisenberg Bell time T ≥ π/8; the explicit trajectory e^{−iHT}|01⟩ is an analytic computation in the paper, not a Lean statement

statements.title: the IBM chip-to-chip transfer: 80 cm coax, one standing mode, g/2π = 8–9 MHz, T_g = 256–312 ns, F = 98.86–99.29 %
certified floor: T ≥ π/(2√2 g) for the relay, from the any-dimension speed limit with ‖H‖ ≤ √2 g
statements.formal_part: the angle bound fsAngle ≤ (Ω/2)·T for piecewise-constant Hamiltonians in any dimension, applied with shift c = 0 and Ω/2 = √2 g; the norm ‖H‖ = (|g₁|² + |g₂|²)^{1/2} and the angle π/2 of the transfer are the paper’s one-line application

statements.title: the single-mode minimal time is π/(√2 g) (Boscain–Chambrion–Charlot 2005); its lower half gT ≥ π/√2 is machine-checked in Isabelle
Table VII: the IBM transfers last 5.8–7.9× the single-mode minimal time (4.1–5.6× sequential, 11.6–15.9× the certified floor); the 126 ns target would still be 2.9–3.2×

at the minimal time the coherence error of the optimal protocol is 0.13–0.26 % (master equation), 4–6× below the measured errors; IBM’s additive model gives less (0.09–0.17 %): exact for relaxation, not for dephasing; one protocol, not a floor
caveats: many cable modes (the bounds then hold with the collective norm G), g is the maximal coupling, IBM’s fidelity and error model, Markovian dephasing at the Ramsey rate
the certified objects are the inequalities, not the gaps; the bounds not in Lean and the truncation are listed

the abstract: 11.3× at full amplitude, ≈ 2× at the drive IBM uses, gates ≈ 10× faster than the median within each device’s full amplitude, 4.22× for two qubits, a CZ between 0.295 and 0.331 of the qubit-only time (version 3)
what the paper claims: five contributions (the fifth in version 2), and no new physics
every number traces to a script of the companion package, linked from this blueprint

conclusion: 11.3× at full amplitude and ≈ 2× at the drive used; X gates ≈ 10× faster than the median within the full amplitude (4.8 ns at r_full); 4.22× for two qubits; a CZ between the two-copy bound 0.4632/J and the certified protocol 0.5200/J (version 3)
